 Barabas  
 
 
 Barabas is the solo project of Hungarian trumpeter and composer Lőrinc Barabás. Blending trumpet, piano, synthesizers, and electronics, his music moves between neoclassical, ambient, contemporary jazz, and electronic music, creating a cinematic sound world built around strong melodies, improvisation, and atmospheric textures. Over a career spanning nearly two decades, Barabás has released twelve albums across solo and ensemble projects. His solo catalogue includes Sastra (2013), Elevator Dance Music (2015), Algorhythms (2019), and the intimate, piano-centered 22 (2023). His latest album, Orbit (2026), develops this musical language further, bringing minimalist piano, atmospheric synthesizers, electronic rhythms, and trumpet into a more spacious and meditative setting. As a live artist, Barabas transforms this material into an immersive solo performance, moving fluidly between piano, trumpet, synthesizers, looping, and electronics. Rather than separating acoustic and electronic music, he uses them as parts of the same musical language, allowing composed pieces and improvisation to evolve naturally on stage. Barabás has toured extensively throughout Europe and the United States, opened for Jean-Michel Jarre, and collaborated with artists including Erik Truffaz, Takuya Kuroda, Niklas Paschburg, and Valerie June. International appearances include the EFG London Jazz Festival at the Barbican, Brooklyn Public Library, The Town Hall in New York, Expo 2020 Dubai, and Expo 2025 Osaka. Performing his solo project under the name Barabas, he brings together nearly two decades of musical exploration in a distinctive contemporary identity — trumpet, piano, and electronics meeting somewhere between the concert hall, jazz club, and electronic stage.

He was awarded full-tuition scholarships to study at Berklee College of Music for both undergraduate and graduate degrees, earning his graduate degree from the extremely exclusive Berklee Global Jazz Institute under the direction of master pianist, educator and humanitarian Danilo Perez. An equally important part of his education was down the street from Berklee at Boston’s historic Wally’s Jazz Cafe. He has also toured around the US, Canada, Europe and China. Herskovits has recorded many albums as a sideman, featured on labels such as Newvelle and Endectomorph music, alongside musicians such Grammy award-winning guitarist Bill Frisell, Michael Blake and Jason Palmer.  A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination,  Jerry Bergonzi  has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. —  By Scott Yanow, AllMusic

 The Fringe  originally formed back in 1971 by tenor-saxophonist  George Garzone , bassist Richard Appleman, and drummer Bob Gullotti as an outlet for their free jazz improvisations, The Fringe have entertained and enlightened Boston area jazz audiences for over 50 years. Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist  John Lockwood . Bob Gullotti passed away in 2020 and is remembered as one of the greatest jazz drummers of his generation. Francisco Mela, now on drums,  graciously fills the space Bob left behind. Along with their impressive tenure with The Fringe, Garzone, Lockwood, and Mela are in great demand as session players and have played with many of the greats of contemporary jazz. Along with keeping up with a busy performance schedule, each of them are well-respected educators helping to inspire the jazz musicians of tomorrow. events.title: Orkest
events.description:
Founded in 2022 by Sapphire Skye Toth and Michael Gehman while they earned their Master of Science degrees in Arts Administration at Boston University, Orkest is meant to be the place where New Music meets The Community and The Community meets New Music.

Orkest, a visionary musical venture rooted in the bustling city of Boston, is on a mission to redefine the local music scene. Recognizing the abundance of untapped musical talent, Orkest seeks to bridge the gap between emerging composers and the community, breaking away from classical traditions and creating an inviting space for diverse genres. Departing from conventional models, Orkest utilizes venues to bring people to music, not just vice versa, fostering a casual environment in cafe bars and libraries. With a commitment to equitable treatment of artists, creating opportunities for artists at socioeconomic disadvantages, professional recordings of performances, and a unique pay-what-you-wish model, Orkest is not just a music experience; it's a transformative force shaping how communities engage with and appreciate new music and the artists who create it.

events.description:
$10 admission / 7pm / seated show Jesse Gallagher  began living above the Lilypad in 2006, just a few blocks from where his grandfather grew up on Inman st.  At the time Jesse was in the middle of what would be about a decade of regular touring, performing & recording with his psychedelic rock band Apollo Sunshine.  The band was featured in the New York Times, Rolling Stone, Spin & shared the stage with legendary acts  Wu-Tang Clan ,  Toots & The Maytals ,  The Flaming Lips  &  Dr. Dog . Jesse has been involved with the Lilypad for 20 years and the full time talent booking agent since 2013. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Breaking Bad used Jesse’s song “We are Born When We Die” (2008) to dramatic effect. “Today is the Day” (2005) was in international Nike commercials while his “Singing to the Earth to Thank Her For You” was used in a large GAP campaign. Gallagher has collaborated, recorded & performed extensively w/  Sam Cohen ,  Willy Mason ,  Lilys ,  Nick Nicely ,  Doug Tuttle  &  Edan . Gallagher is a certified Yoga & Meditation teacher and hosts classes at the Lilypad & online. Since 2018, he has released 40 pieces of instrumental music which have been used in millions of YouTube videos ranging from NBC NY to Tesla and most recently a string of viral videos by Emma Chamberlain. Gallagher has a very active YouTube channel, making lots of psychedelic music videos and building a community of mindful listeners. @jessegallagher.tv Steve Fell  is a guitarist, composer, and educator whose performing and recording career over the last twenty five years has reached across the boundaries of jazz, experimental, funk, free form improvisation, rock, electronic, reggae/calypso, hip-hop, psych, and many others.   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 He co-leads the groups  Clear Audience, Quantum Banditos, Dome Room,  and  Astronomico,  leads a trio under his own name, and collaborates with numerous bands and artists. @stevefellmusic

 The Fringe  originally formed back in 1971 by tenor-saxophonist  George Garzone , bassist Richard Appleman, and drummer Bob Gullotti as an outlet for their free jazz improvisations, The Fringe have entertained and enlightened Boston area jazz audiences for over 50 years. Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist  John Lockwood . Bob Gullotti passed away in 2020 and is remembered as one of the greatest jazz drummers of his generation. Francisco Mela, now on drums,  graciously fills the space Bob left behind. Along with their impressive tenure with The Fringe, Garzone, Lockwood, and Mela are in great demand as session players and have played with many of the greats of contemporary jazz. Along with keeping up with a busy performance schedule, each of them are well-respected educators helping to inspire the jazz musicians of tomorrow. events.title: TCS presents: Sarah Adelman
events.description:
18+ w/ 2-Item Suggested Minimum. Doors at 630pm / Show at 730pm. Please Arrive Early to Guarantee Seating.
Sarah Adelman
 will headline The Comedy Studio for one night only on her Office Hours tour! Sarah is a stand up comedian and award-winning writer born and raised in NYC. She’s opened for Janeane Garofalo, Judy Gold, Pete Lee, and Mohanad Elsheiky, and tours nationwide. Sarah was named a 2026 Comedian to Watch by Gold Comedy and created and stars in 
Blow My Mind,
 a breakout science series on MadRealities with over 150 million views. Her sitcom pilot was an official selection for JFL Speed Pitching and she's taped original specials for LMAOF and Levity Live for the Brooklyn Improv.  She was recently featured in the 
New York Times
. You can follow Sarah at
@sarahadelman1
 on instagram or read more about her at 
www.sarahadelmancomedy.com

events.title: TCS presents: Eddie Pepitone
events.description:
18+ w/ 2-Item Suggested Minimum.
Eddie Pepitone is a master of the dark art of comedy. Hailed as a modern day cross between Jackie Gleason, Don Rickles and Eckhart Tolle. Eddie is a force of nature on stage, switching between social rage and self-doubt. His shows are an energetic combo of calm and chaos, blue-collar angst and sardonic enlightenment. Few comedians working today channel the power of the rant better than Eddie Pepitone. Eddie's latest stand-up special, 
The Collapse
,
 is out now on streaming platform VEEPS and YouTube. The special is a true Pepitone rant and romp as he barrels through the heightened emotions and anxieties of modern life in a somehow joyful and jovial energy that only Pepitone can deliver. Eddie's stand-up special prior to this, 
For the Masses
,
 was released in June 2020 and was named amongst the Best Comedy of 2020 by the 
New York Times
.
Host: 
Andrew Balestieri

events.title: Maison Électronique
events.description:
Maison Électronique is an instrumental trio playing original 
compositions that blend Congolese rumba and contemporary seben guitar 
styles with other African musics and Western styles like shoegaze, surf,
 and dub. The group is led by guitarist Nathaniel Braddock. Braddock has
 traveled extensively in West and Central Africa, and collaborated with 
many musicians from Ghana, Congo, Zambia, Uganda, Mali, Mozambique, and 
Senegal, as well as US and Australian Indie rock bands. He
 is joined by Ugandan bassist Alex Donsal Kateregga and drummer Frank 
Aveni. The group gets compared to vibey instrumental guitar trios Khruangbin and La Lom,but with more notes.

events.title: JAZZ NIGHT: Dave Fox Trio
events.description:
The Dave Fox Trio is a Modern Jazz Trio featuring original jazz
compositions and arrangements inspired by artists such as John Coltrane, Joe Henderson, Chick Corea, Steve Swallow, Charles Mingus, Thelonious Monk and Wayne Shorter. The group features internationally acclaimed bassist John Lockwood and innovative Boston area musicians and composers such as guitarist Phil Sargent and saxophonists Nicholas Brust and Bill Jones.

Dave Fox is an accomplished, versatile drummer and is currently a full-time member of The Gravel Project, Dan Rockett and The Guilty Party and
“AS3” along with Andrew Stern and Brad Barrett.

As a sideman for over two decades, he has performed with a diverse group of artists including Jerry Bergonzi, John Lockwood, Josh Smith, Dave Tronzo, Charles Neville, Stan Strickland, The Stompers and Tom Hambridge and The Rattlesnakes to name a few.

events.description:
18+ w/ 2-Item Suggested Minimum. Please Arrive Early to Guarantee Seating.
Shafi Hossain
 is a New York City-based stand-up comedian, writer, and producer. Originally from Bangladesh, he moved to the United States to study chemical engineering before falling in love with standup comedy. Now a regular performer at the prestigious Comedy Cellar, Shafi has established himself as a prominent voice in the NYC comedy scene. He was named one of "New York's Funniest Stand Ups" by the New York Comedy Festival and has been featured on Kevin Hart’s LOL Network series Road Comics on Peacock. Shafi has toured internationally—headlining shows in London, Paris, Bangladesh, and Canada.

events.title: JAZZ NIGHT: Bill Jones Trio
events.description: Bill Jones, a native of Marion, Massachusetts, is a tenor and soprano saxophonist that been a regular on the jazz scene since he moved to Boston in 1999 to study at the New England Conservatory. He is inspired by such greats as Joe Henderson, John Coltrane, Hank Mobley, Wayne Shorter, and Charlie Parker, as well as modern masters like Jerry Bergonzi, George Garzone, Joe Lovano, Joshua Redman, and Mark Turner. Bill regularly plays at venues in and around Boston, such as Wally’s, The Beehive, Monkfish, and Lilypad. He enjoys playing classic and modern jazz standards and his original compositions. He has performed with many revered jazz musicians, such as Bob Gullotti, Leo Genovese, Herb Pomeroy, Jeff Galindo, Tim Ray, Greg Hopkins, and John Lockwood.

Wind down your weekend with "Sunday Best", a premier weekly stand-up comedy showcase, lovingly curated by Jeff Zamaria (LFM Comedy), featuring THE BEST in Boston comedy with a different headliner. Katie Arroyo
 is aggressively funny and fearlessly honest when it comes to all things relationships. A New England-based comic with roots in the Boston scene, she’s a standout from the Boston Comedy Festival and the Rogue Island Comedy Festival. Katie has toured with the hilarious Jiaoying Summers and the iconic Natasha Leggero.

events.title: The Space Consortium's Space Table
events.description:
Whether you're a space professional, student, educator, science communicator, longtime space enthusiast, or simply curious about space, come enjoy an informal evening of conversation, games, and new connections.

The Space Table is our new monthly gathering bringing together Space Consortium Members (MA-based space academics and professionals) and Explorers (space enthusiasts) for space and science conversations, board games, discussions, and more. What happens at The Space Table will be shaped by you: share what you're working on, pick a space or science topic to discuss, join a game, meet someone with completely different expertise, and tell us what you'd like to see at future gatherings.

No space background or expertise is required. Everyone is welcome!
Free and open to all: Registration is free, but spots are limited, so register now to reserve yours.

events.title: TCS presents: Liam Nelson
events.description:
18+ w/ 2-Item Suggested Minimum. Doors at 5pm / Show at 6pm. Please Arrive Early to Guarantee Seating.
Liam Nelson
 is a New York City-based comedian hailing from Atlanta, Georgia. Standing an impressive 7 feet tall and living with Marfan Syndrome, Liam offers a unique perspective on life as a "walking spectacle." At just 26 years old, he weaves sharp, hilarious commentary on navigating the world as a disabled young adult with stories that are equal parts outrageous and deeply relatable. He’s headlined nationwide along with performing with top comics like Sam Morril, Gianmarco Soresi and Dusty Slay, appeared at the Netflix Is A Joke festival, and released his first Dry Bar Comedy Special in 2025. He also appeared on the 2026 season of Netflix’s Star Search Reboot.
Feature: 
Ty Colgate

events.title: TCS presents: Sean Patton
events.description:
18+ w/ 2-Item Suggested Minimum.
Sean Patton
 is a comedian based in New York, by way of New Orleans. He began doing stand-up in the Crescent City and has since performed in comedy clubs and festivals across the world, including The Melbourne International Comedy Festival (2011, 2018), The Glasgow Comedy Festival (2016), the Dublin Comedy fest (2017), and The Edinburgh Fringe (2017, 2019). Other festival appearances include SXSW (2016, 2017, 2018, 2022), The Moontower Comedy Festival (2012, 2013, 2014, 2019), Just for Laughs Chicago (2013), Just for Laughs Toronto (2013), and Just for Laughs Montreal (2008, 2010, 2012, 2016, 2018). He's performed on Comedy Central’s 
Live at Gotham
 (2009), 
Late Night with Jimmy Fallon
 (2010), 
Conan
 (2011, 2013), and Comedy Central’s 
The Half Hour 
(2013). More recently, He's been on 
@midnight
 (2014, 2015), 
The Meltdown with Jonah and Kumail 
(2015), 
This Is Not Happening
 (2015, 2017, 2019), Showtime's 
Live from SXSW 
(2017), TruTv's 
Comedy Knockout
 (2016, 2017, 2018), and 
This week at the Comedy Cellar 
(2018, 2019, 2020). In 2019, he released his second album, "
Scuttlebutt", 
on Helium Records. His next album 
King Scorpio, 
was released on Christmas Eve 2021 and as a special on YouTube in August 2022. His special 
Number One 
streamed on Peacock from 2022 to 2024 and is currently available on 800lb Gorilla’s YouTube page. As for acting, He's appeared on IFC's 
Maron, 
Comedy Central's 
Inside Amy Schumer, 
and TruTV's 
Those Who Can't. 
He stars alongside Brian Jordan Alvarez, Stephanie Koenig, Enrico Colantoni, and Carmen Christopher in two seasons of FX’s 
English Teacher

events.title: Ricky Stein
events.description: Austin-born singer/songwriter Ricky Stein writes songs that seek to find spiritual common ground between the mesas of West Texas and the streetscapes of the world's great music capitals. Original compositions such as "Night Shines On," "American Dreaming," and "The Great Empty" capture the energy of urban life in the modern era; latest single "Heart of the Night" seeks hope and meaning through human connection. All songs are delivered in an earnest baritone accompanied by acoustic guitar, harmonica, and a good-humored stage presence.

events.title: Chuck Clough

In 2016, Chuck founded and hosted (with musician Ronnie Hirschberg) the award-winning podcast Above The Basement - Boston Music and Conversation, which won a 202o Boston Music Award for Podcast/Radio Show of the Year.  After 200 episodes, Chuck shuttered the podcast and set out on his solo musical endeavor. 

 He currently performs in New England and is always on the lookout for the lost songs that have influenced him over the years.

past_events.title: Lilypad Jazz Jam
past_events.description:
$5 - 15 sliding scale admission / 4 - 7pm / all ages 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 We're excited to be welcoming the community into our space to play and listen to music together.  The Lilypad Jazz Jam is open to instrumentalists of all levels, we only ask that you come prepared to play at least one or two well known Jazz Standards in the commonly played key. And of course listeners are welcome to come and enjoy the music these spontaneously arranged ensembles will create! Our host will be working with players to make sure everyone gets a chance to get on stage and play something they're comfortable with. We'll have a drum kit, piano, upright bass and guitar/bass amplifiers on the back line. Our stage hosts some of the heaviest players on the planet, come down and catch the vibe! We have Nic Adams hosting and leading the band to get the night started. Come early, you won't want to miss their performance! Nic Adams  is a multi-instrumentalist, performer, composer, educator, and luthier based in Boston, MA. Specializing in saxophone, drums, guitar, bass, and north Asian folk music, their music pulls from a long list of traditions, from John Coltrane to punk rock and Tuvan throat singing. With this wide array of influences, Nic seeks to create music that synthesizes many different musical points into a cohesive and unique form. Finding common grounds among musical cultures and using them as jumping-off points for new compositions or improvisations is at the core of Nic’s work. Nic is currently pursuing a Master’s at Longy School of Music, gigs in the greater Boston area, and spends their free time building hybrid Tuvan/western traditional instruments. Please direct any questions to  persistentfool@protonmail.com

past_events.title: Wheated Rivalry: A Heated Rivalry-themed variety show
past_events.description: TICKETS AVAILABLE HERE Join New Normal Comedy & Read My Lips Boston for an evening celebrating Heated Rivalry (and raising $$ for LUCE) at Idle Hands Craft Ales! Brought to you by Idle Hands Craft Ales, New Normal Comedy, and Read My Lips Boston,  WHEATED RIVALRY  is back! Join us (and your fellow Loons) for a Heated Rivalry-themed variety show with a portion of ticket proceeds going to LUCE to fight ICE! An individual ticket gets you entry into the comedy show, plus a complimentary drink token (redeemable for either a non-alcoholic or alcoholic beverage at Idle Hands). You’ll also be able to browse diverse books and bookish merch at Read My Lips Boston's romance bookshop pop-up! MEET YOUR HOSTS About Idle Hands Craft Ales Idle Hands has always been about bringing people together around great beer. On the brew deck, in the cellar or at the taps, their staff all share a love for both timeworn recipes and bold twists. In their Malden taproom, their patrons gather to see old friends and make new ones. Idle Hands is committed to the very ground that our foundation stands on. Through local events, neighborhood cleanups, fundraising and more, they are always looking for ways to give back to the city and its people. About New Normal Comedy New Normal Comedy is redefining the comedy scene in New England by creating inclusive spaces where humor meets humanity. They aim to make the stage feel like home, fostering environments where comics can thrive and audiences can connect. By highlighting underrepresented voices, New Normal brings together people who haven’t always been made to feel "normal," ensuring everyone finds their place in the laughter. About Read My Lips Boston Read My Lips Boston is a diverse romance bookshop that partners with breweries, cafes, and other establishments to host monthly mobile shops all around Boston. Their curated selection of love stories centers authors and main characters identifying as BIPOC, disabled, queer, big-bodied, and members of other groups historically underrepresented in the romance genre. Read My Lips donates 10% of their proceeds to local and national non-profits and social causes. TICKETS AVAILABLE HERE

$15 admission / 10pm doors / 10:30 show / all ages Katie Rugg & the Kites, Skategoat, and Holes in Socks invite you to join them for a night of original indie/alt rock filled with groovy guitar riffs, catchy melodies, and introspective storytelling.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Holes in Socks   
 
 
 is a five-piece alternative rock band based in Boston, MA. Their songs are inspired by the rich grunge and pop-punk tunes of the 2000s, while also drawing on indie rock from the early 2020s. Their artistic influences include Paramore, Fall Out Boy, Fountains of Wayne, beabadoobee, and Beach Bunny. With a lighthearted, passionate stage presence, their songs explore gut-wrenching interpersonal experiences, struggles in the music industry, and occasional pastimes that distract from these troubles. holesinsocksband.carrd.co 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Skategoat 
 
 
 Formed at Berklee College of Music in 2025, Skategoat is a four-person indie rock band based in Boston, MA. Skategoat mixes hard-hitting lyrics with a dynamic sound for anyone around to listen. The music of Skategoat draws influence from the Backseat Lovers and Peach Pit. IG:  @skategoat.theband 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Katie Rugg & the Kites 
 
 
 With her kaleidoscopic sound and intricate lyrics, Katie Rugg can only be described as esoteric. Drawing on inspiration from artists like Pink Floyd, Bob Dylan, and the Beatles, Katie Rugg’s songwriting isn’t bound by genre. From high-energy psych-rock anthems to somber folk ballads, Katie Rugg and her band will have you laughing, crying, and dancing until the sun comes up. www.katierugg.com

past_events.title: Lafayette Gilchrist ft. Cecil Brooks of the Sun Ra Arkestra
past_events.description:
$25 at the door / $20 in advance / $15 students and seniors / 7:30 doors / seated 
 
 
 
 
    Get Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 
 Lafayette Gilchrist featuring special guest and Cambridge native, Cecil Brooks of the Sun Ra Arkestra. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Lafayette Gilchrist’s music draws on the span of jazz history from stride to free improvisation, along with inspiration from hip-hop, funk, and Washington D.C.’s unique go-go sound. His work thrives on making surprising connections between styles and influences, boldly veering from piledriver funk to piquant stride, vigorous swing to hip-hop swagger, contemplative abstraction to deep-bottom grooves. Gilchrist is the pianist in the Sun Ra Arkestra, has toured extensively with David Murray, and his compositions have graced the soundtracks of David Simon’s acclaimed series The Wire, The Deuce, and Treme. Gilchrist has performed with Cassandra Wilson, Macy Gray, Oliver Lake, Andrew Cyrille, Orrin Evans, Paul Dunmall, Hamid Drake, William Parker and many more. Gilchrist’s second solo recording, 2019 “Dark Matter” which muses on the elusive and mysterious matter that ties the universe together, landed on numerous critics best of lists. Gilchrist returns to The Lilypad, where he played for a standing room only crowd in 2022, for a performance featuring a special guest appearance by Cambridge native and fellow member of the Sun Ra Arkestra, Cecil Brooks on trumpet. www.lafayettegilchrist.com

past_events.title: Indie Wonderland
past_events.description:
$15 at the door / $12 online / 10:15 doors / 10:30 show / all ages Isaac Martin, Catherine Claire, & Joey Jr join for a night of Indie & Alternative music at The Lilypad! Indie Wonderland is a vibrant night filled with the most exciting upcoming indie artists that Boston has to offer. From high energy indie pop to indie folk and alternative, all types of indie fanatics leave with a new favorite artist! 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Isaac Martin 
 
 
 Isaac Martin is a high-energy indie pop artist who loves to wear his heart on his sleeve. Through vulnerable lyrics and engaging performances, his music nurtures a powerful emotional connection with the listener. Additionally, Isaac is a seasoned performer, having performed at historic venues/events such as SummerFest (MIL), The Rave / Eagles Club (MIL), White Oak Music Hall (HTX), Warehouse Live (HTX), and The Lilypad (BOS) in front of hundreds of people. Officially launching his solo project in September 2026 with his debut single “None of That Matters Now”, Isaac is looking to take the Indie Pop world by storm through his growing list of live performances & releases. wixsite.com/isaacmartinmusic   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Catherine Claire 
 
 
 Catherine Claire is an Asian-American artist and producer based in Boston, MA. She draws from her past experiences within her music, and seeks to connect with her listeners through her lyrical storytelling. Her music often blends elements of indie pop, indie rock, and folk, creating a sound that feels both intimate and experimental. catherineclairemusic.com 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Joey Jr. 
 
 
 Using his fondness for nature, Joey forges folk music that implements flora and fauna acting as a layer of romanticism, as well as hints of religious imagery. Hailing from the suburbs of Wisconsin, Joey uses Indie Folk and Alternative music platforms for talking about queer love with a midwest lens. past_events.description:
$20 admission / $15 for students and seniors / 1:45 doors / 2pm start New Music for the 21 piece Jazz Orchestra by resident composers David Harris, Darrell Katz, Bob Pilkington and Mimi Rabson. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 The Jazz Composers Alliance was founded in 41 years ago to support, develop and promote the art of music composition in the jazz idiom.   The JCA Orchestra  was founded to realize that goal, and it has been a fixture on Boston’s creative music scene ever since its first performance in December 1985. The JCA Orchestra has released 12 critically acclaimed CDs.  Wheelworks  was on Downbeat’s Best of 2016 list.  The group has performed (and on a few occasions, recorded with) an illustrious group of guest performer/composers, including Sam Rivers, Julius Hemphill, Dave Holland, Maria Schneider, Henry Threadgill, Steve Lacy and Oliver Lake. Drawing on influences that span the history of jazz and the world's musical traditions, the JCA Orchestra has brought together a huge palette of sounds, structures and concepts. This group has premiered well over 125 pieces. Our concepts include extended forms, group improvisation from a variety of approaches, notated and not notated music, and striving to combine composition and improvisation in new ways. The 21-piece JCA orchestra a string trio, a vocalist, as well as a full-time flute player,  and French horn, we’re not a typical big band, We have lasted since 1985, and it’s because we have a like-minded group of people who love making music, who are committed to stretching boundaries, and write and perform with joy and passion. JCA performances have variety, adventure, and a great communal feel. “The band plays with drive and vitality. the soloists responding with imaginative fire to the charts and the ensemble. This is contemporary big band music of a very high order, written and played with considerable skill and integrity”- swing2bop.com/reviews . “It is a remarkable feat to keep a big band such as this one going for as long as it has, and the result is a tightly presented sonance that any lover of the larger aggregates should appreciate”-gapplegate   “The versatility of the band is breathtaking, ranging from moody blues to ear splitting bouts of cacophonic climaxes” Borderland

past_events.title: UPSTAIRS: Somerville Songwriter Sessions
past_events.description:
Learn more / Buy Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 As it has for more than a decade, Somerville Songwriter Sessions presents the finest acoustic singer-songwriters each month in an intimate, welcoming setting. Each concert features three songwriters each doing a solo set, and then trading songs in the round, allowing for stories, impromptu harmonies, jamming, and spontaneous inspiration. Each show, one of our five hosts – Rachel Marie, Terry Kitchen, Sam Bayer, Beth DeSombre, Jack Byrne – are joined by some of the best local and touring singer-songwriters on the scene. November 8: Rachel Marie Rachel Marie (she/they) follows in a tradition of unapologetically forthright femme folksingers, with songs that hearken to "overstuffed lines of Tori Amos, philosophical turn of Indigo Girls, and lilting vocals like Joni Mitchell" (Victoria Farmer, The Christian Humanist Podcast). The social awareness of folk meets the introspection and healing of the singer-songwriter tradition, featuring the emotional catharsis and dynamic vocals of a Broadway show. With a songwriting approach as raw and honest as it's always been, Rachel Marie is making a return to live performance after an unintentional hibernation hiatus, ready to reconnect with a real live audience. December 13: Beth DeSombre Beth DeSombre writes songs that are "smart and  uplifting...focusing on the quiet meaning to be found in ordinary life" (Sing Out! Magazine), exploring issues from the personal to the political. Her music touches both mind and heart, with insights wrapped in melody and harmony that stay with you after the echoes of the last chorus have faded away. Her newest CD Holding the Threads (2024) is her most personal album to date, telling stories about family and crisis and trying to find hope in dark times. Her previous EP The Sea Beside Us (2023), tells stories of ships and the ocean. Her 2017 EP Resistance, which was written in response to the political situation after the 2016 election, is a fundraiser for the ACLU. An award-winning writer in many formats, she has published 8 books. $15 in advance. (+ processing fees) $20 at the door. This Is An All Ages Show Doors are at 3:30pm. Showtime is 4pm. Dinner and drinks available at all tables. NO REFUNDS OR EXCHANGES

past_events.title: Kass Richards + Chris Brokaw
past_events.description: $10-$15 sliding scale admission / 7pm doors / 7:45 show / seated & standing Kass Richards EP release show with special guest Chris Brokaw. Richards will be accompanied by a full band for the first time ever locally. Brokaw, who played multiple instruments on the Richards EP, will be performing one of his characteristically hypnotic solo sets to close out the evening.  Double-click to edit... Kass Richards Kass Richards grew up in rural Virginia and currently resides in the Boston area. Her new EP, Gospel, is out November 6, 2026. The four-song album was crafted over three sessions with Chris Brokaw (Come, Codeine, The Lemonheads) and David Minehan (The Neighborhoods, The Replacements); the latter also co-produced the album with Richards. Recorded in the aftermath of intense personal loss, Gospel is imbued with the shapeshifting emotions that come from grief, as well as a strong gratitude and reverence for things lost. The EP explores many sides of Richards' artistry, expanding her creative vision through inspiration from past collaborators. Gospel follows the 2024 release of Richards’ second full-length album, New Love Meditation, described by Bandcamp as “a work of haunting indie folk.” Richards’ first solo album, The Language Shadow, was released in 2020. Co-produced by Richards and Basia Bulat and recorded at Montreal’s storied Hotel2Tango, The Language Shadow is one of timeless honesty, providing a spare, at times eerie updating on a classical approach. Richards has been a frequent collaborator with Meg Remy and her ever-evolving art pop project, U.S. Girls, contributing backing vocals for Remy’s live band(s) and for the acclaimed Bless This Mess (2023), Heavy Light (2020), and In a Poem Unlimited (2018), all released under 4AD. Richards served as editor for Meg Remy’s first book, Begin by Telling (Book*hug Press, 2021), and created the score for Pottero, an animated short film directed by Lindsey Martin that has since screened at over thirty-five national and international film festivals. Gospel by Kass Richards Chris Brokaw Chris Brokaw is perhaps best known for his work with the bands Codeine and Come. He has released over two dozen solo albums of instrumental and vocal music since 2002, and played in The New Year, Pullman, Consonant, Charnel Ground and the Lemonheads. He has scored nine films, most recently 'Crookedfinger' by Julia Halperin and Jason Cortlund, and written for dance and arts associations, most recently 'Lowlands' with Rimi/Imir in Stavangar, Norway. He has recorded and performed as an accompanist to Thurston Moore, Christina Rosenvinge, Rhys Chatham, Alan Licht, Beth Kaplan, Jennifer O'Connor, Steve Wynn and GG Allin. Currently he plays in Lupa Citta (with Sarah Black and Jenn Gori), the Martha's Vineyard Ferries (with Bob Weston and Elisha Wiesner) and the Chris Brokaw Rock Band (with Clint Conley and Luther Gray). His new duo with Tanya Donelly recently released a record of medieval music, "The Undone Is Done Again', on Fire Records. He continues to perform periodically with Codeine and Come. chrisbrokaw.com

He was awarded full-tuition scholarships to study at Berklee College of Music for both undergraduate and graduate degrees, earning his graduate degree from the extremely exclusive Berklee Global Jazz Institute under the direction of master pianist, educator and humanitarian Danilo Perez. An equally important part of his education was down the street from Berklee at Boston’s historic Wally’s Jazz Cafe. He began going to jam sessions there in high school and eventually became the house bass player every Friday and Saturday night. Ridley has played and recorded with renowned musicians of many different styles all over the world.  An incredibly versatile multi-instrumentalist, Max performs regularly in bands playing Jazz, Rock, Folk, Soul, Punk, Klezmer, Polka and every other style you can think of.  He also serves as the music director for tap dance company Subject:Matter ( https://www.subjectmattertap.com/ ) and teaches music as a guest lecturer at different colleges around New England (such as Longy School of Music, University of New Hampshire and Berklee College of Music).  A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination,  Jerry Bergonzi  has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. —  By Scott Yanow, AllMusic

past_events.description:
$35 admission / 10pm doors / 10:15 music / all ages Peruvian born drummer, percussionist and composer,  Jorge Perez-Albela  is presenting an unforgettable evening of music improvisation with world class jazz masters, pianist  Kenny Werner  and bassist  John Lockwood.   Kenny Werner: piano John Lockwood: bass Jorge Perez-Albela: drums  Kenny Werner Kenny has been a world-class pianist and composer for over forty years. His prolific output of compositions, recordings and publications continue to impact audiences around the world. In 1996 he wrote his landmark book,  Effortless Mastery, Liberating The Master Musician Within . Werner has  since created videos, lectured world-wide and authored many articles on how musicians, artists or even business people can allow their “master creator” within to lift their performance to it’s highest level, showing us how to be spontaneous, fearless, joyful and disciplined in our work and in our life. Kenny was awarded the 2010 Guggenheim Fellowship Award for his seminal work,  No Beginning No End . No Beginning No End is a musical journey exploring tragedy and loss, death and transition, and the path from one lifetime to the next. Utilizing over 70 musicians, Kenny’s third album for Half Note Records is an expansive composition featuring Joe Lovano, Judy Silvano, Wind Ensemble, Choir and String Quartet. Born in Brooklyn, NY on November 19, 1951 and then growing up in Oceanside, Long Island, Kenny began playing and performing at a young age, first recording on television at the age of 11. Although he studied classical piano as a child, he enjoyed playing anything he heard on the radio. In high school and his first years of college he attended the Manhattan School of Music as a classical piano major. His natural instinct for improvisation led Kenny to the Berklee School of Music in 1970. There he sought tutelage of the renowned piano teacher Madame Chaloff. A Her gracious wisdom and inspiration became a driving force in Kenny’s conception: A music conscious of its spiritual intent and essence. From Boston, Kenny traveled to Brazil with the saxophonist Victor Assis Brasil. There he met Victor’s twin brother, Brazilian pianist Joao Assis Brasil. He studied with Joao, who provided another piece of the puzzle for Kenny’s conception that would lead to Effortless Mastery, his landmark opus on how to allow the master musician from within to manifest.  www.kennywerner.com John Lockwood John Lockwood was born in Cape Town South Africa. Lockwood moved to the United States in 1973, where he studied at Berklee College of Music with Bill Curtis, Henry Portnoi, and Arthur Webb until 1978.
